checks: Source c1694074e553a581, The densities are not power-concave, uses the identical cube product and coordinates 49/100 and 53/100. The frozen proof strengthens it to every density representative by a null-set argument.

The compact convex product has strict-side fibers at distances 1 and 2, both equal to K. Their Jacobians are 1 and 2^d, and their direction images K and K/2 are nested, giving the two positive density values and convex superlevels.

The first test point is strictly inside K/2 and the other two evaluation points have first coordinates 53/100 and 51/100, strictly between 1/2 and 1. All values hold on small open neighborhoods. At equal weights each finite power mean of 1 and 1+2^d exceeds 1, including the geometric mean and negative exponents.

If N is the null exceptional set of a new representative, pairs with either endpoint in N have product measure zero. For each fixed first endpoint, the midpoint map in the second is affine invertible, so pairs with midpoint in N also have measure zero. Thus a violating pair exists in the chosen open product for every representative.
